subject: Homebrew cmdstan install available (and cmdstan build/install structure)

messages.author: 7f3dcb786c576e61
messages.subject: Homebrew cmdstan install available (and cmdstan build/install structure)
parts:
Hi,

I have updated the Homebrew formula for installing cmdstan and had it accepted by the Homebrew maintainers. This means that Mac OS X users with homebrew can now install cmdstan simply by running:

brew install cmdstan

on a command line.

When creating the homebrew formula I had to rewrite the cmdstan make files in order to build files into the directory structure that Homebrew enforces. I'm not sure of the reasons for why cmdstan build object files into the bin dir (and related issues, see link to formula below) but I suggest long-term this might be changed to use a more standard build/directory structure. Please see this formula file for the 3 rewrite steps I had to introduce to build into "lib" rather than the "bin" dir (for non-binary files):

https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-science/blob/master/cmdstan.rb

A more detailed account of the steps I went through to get this past Homebrew maintainers can be found here:
https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-science/pull/3215

Best regards,

Robert Feldt

messages.author: 7f3dcb786c576e61
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Homebrew cmdstan install available (and cmdstan build/install structure)
parts:
Thanks!

Personally I use stan via Stan.jl so I may not represent the typical use case/scenario here => I have not changed this. If you have a proposal for how to do this simpler we can probably fix it in a future update. The simplest might be to include a new makestan command in the cmdstan homebrew install that you can run from any directory and it will "know" about the needed paths and flags and build things for you.

For now you can run

brew test cmdstan

to see an example of how to build a model given the changed paths.

Rob
